unavailable: Awak's settings aren't reachable. Check that the Kemudi AI orchestrator is running.

botAccess.title: Awak can't open this project
botAccess.notMember: Awak isn't a member of this project in Taiga, so it can't see the board and no story gets picked up.
botAccess.given: Awak can open this project now
botAccess.askAdmin: Ask a project admin to give Awak access.

status.title: Awak
status.description: When Awak is on, it picks up Ready stories with an area tag, writes the code on a branch, runs the checks and QA, then follows the merge policy below.
status.label: Awak works on this project
status.turnedOn: Awak is on for this project
status.turnedOff: Awak is off. Running jobs finish; no new ones start.

merge.title: Merge policy
merge.description: What happens after Awak finishes a story on its branch. Any failure leaves {{branch}} untouched and tags the story needs-human.
merge.label: Merge into {{branch}}

manual.label: Manual
manual.risk: Awak stops at the branch and tags the story awaiting-merge. Someone on your team reviews and merges outside Kemudi. Nothing reaches {{branch}} without them.

approve.label: Approve
approve.risk: An admin clicks Merge on the story. Kemudi merges into {{branch}}, reruns the checks and pushes, then runs the deploy command. One human look before every merge.

auto.label: Auto
auto.risk: Merges into {{branch}} and runs the deploy command with no human check, right after checks and QA pass on the exact commit. For small or throwaway projects.
auto.needsBrowser: Needs QA set to Browser. Kemudi auto-merges only code that was run and checked in a browser.

confirm.title: Merge without a human check?
confirm.body: Every story that passes QA will be merged into {{branch}} and pushed, and the deploy command will run, without anyone looking first. A bad change can reach production. Use this for small or throwaway projects.

deploy.label: Deploy command
deploy.hintLocal: Runs after each merge in the runner sandbox on Kemudi's server, from the repo's root, without Docker. Leave empty to merge without deploying.
deploy.hintSsh: Runs after each merge on {{host}} over SSH, as {{user}}. Leave empty to merge without deploying.
deploy.set: A deploy command is set. Only project admins can see it.
deploy.notSet: No deploy command is set; merges do not deploy.

qa.label: QA before a story is Done
qa.lockedByAuto: Auto merge needs Browser. Choose Approve or Manual below to lower QA.

off.label: Off
off.help: No checks. The commit is pushed and the story goes to Done for review.

gates.label: Gates only
gates.help: Runs the repo's install, lint, type and test commands. Nothing is opened in a browser.

browser.label: Browser
browser.help: Gates, then Awak starts the app and checks each acceptance criterion in a browser.

llm.title: Model connection (all agents)
llm.description: The OpenAI-compatible provider Awak's agents call, such as sumopod, OpenAI, OpenRouter, DeepSeek, Groq, or a self-hosted vLLM or Ollama.
llm.hierarchy: An agent's own setting comes first, then this one, then the Kemudi server default ({{model}}, {{host}}).
llm.roleDescription: The provider and key this agent calls.
llm.roleClears: Saving removes this agent's own connection and its stored key; it then uses the project's.
llm.roleModelRequired: Pick a model for this agent's own connection.
llm.roleConnFailed: The role was saved, but its model connection wasn't: {{error}}
llm.roleHierarchy: With project default on, this agent uses the project's connection, or else the Kemudi server default ({{model}}, {{host}}).
llm.baseUrlHint: https://, or http:// to a private address for a self-hosted model.
llm.ollamaHint: Ollama must be reachable from the Kemudi AI orchestrator, not only from your computer. host.docker.internal is the machine Docker runs on.
llm.modelHint: Pick from the provider's list, or type any model name it accepts.

models.search: Search or type a model name
models.empty: No models listed. Type a model name to use it.
models.failedShort: The model list didn't load. Type a model name to use it.

llm.keyHintNew: Stored encrypted and never shown again. Leave empty for a self-hosted model that needs no key.
llm.keyHintStored: Stored encrypted. Only the last 4 characters are shown.
llm.keyHintReplace: Replaces the stored key when you save.
llm.keyMoves: The stored key ending in {{last4}} will be sent to this new address. Replace it if it belongs to another provider.

insecure.title: Unencrypted connection
insecure.body: This address uses plain http over the internet. The API key and every prompt, including your client’s code, travel unencrypted, so anyone on the way can read or change them. Prefer https: put a reverse proxy with TLS in front of the model, use a tunnel, or reach it over a private network.
insecure.badgeHint: Plain http to a public address: the API key and prompts travel unencrypted.

clearConfirm.title: Clear this model connection?
clearConfirm.projectBody: The base URL, model and stored key are removed. Agents without their own setting go back to the Kemudi server default.
clearConfirm.roleBody: The base URL, model and stored key are removed. This agent goes back to the project default.

llm.unavailable: The model connection isn't reachable. Check that the Kemudi AI orchestrator is running.

machine.title: Execution machine
machine.description: Where the deploy command runs, and the machine Kemudi checks against the minimum a job needs.
machine.label: Machine
machine.localHint: The runner sandbox on the server Kemudi runs on. Nothing to set up.

remoteNotice.title: Jobs still run on Kemudi's server
remoteNotice.body: You can set up and check an SSH machine now, and the deploy command runs on it. Awak's coding, checks and QA stay on Kemudi's server until remote execution ships.

key.title: Login key
key.hint: Add this public key to {{file}} for the user above on the machine.
key.none: No key yet. Generate one, then add its public key to the machine.

check.needsKey: Generate a key and add it to the machine before checking.
check.oneAtATime: Awak currently works on one story at a time.
check.failed: Below the minimum for one story

hostKey.label: Host key
hostKey.hint: Kemudi trusted this fingerprint on the first connection and refuses the machine if it changes.
hostKey.forgotten: Host key forgotten. The next connection trusts the key it sees.
hostKey.confirmBody: Do this only if you rebuilt or replaced the machine. The next connection will trust whatever key {{host}} presents.

key.generated: Key generated. Only its public half is shown; the private key stays encrypted on the server.
key.regenerateBody: The current key stops working at once. Add the new public key where the old one was before Awak's next job.

repos.title: Repositories
repos.description: The code Awak works on. Each repo gets its own deploy key with write access.
repos.empty: No repositories yet. Add one so Awak has somewhere to work.
repos.created: Repository added. Generate its deploy key next.
repos.deleteBody: Awak stops working on this repo and its deploy key is destroyed. The repo itself is not touched. Roles keep their other repos.

deployKey.title: Deploy key
deployKey.hint: Add this public key as a deploy key with write access on the git host (GitHub: Settings → Deploy keys → Allow write access).
deployKey.localHint: This is Kemudi's own repo on the host, so no deploy key is needed.

checkAccess.title: Access
checkAccess.needsKey: Generate the deploy key and add it to the git host first.
checkAccess.hint: Kemudi lists the branches, fetches {{branch}} and tries a dry-run push. Nothing is written to the remote.
checkAccess.detected: Commands found in the repo: {{fields}}. Empty fields were filled from them.

apps.hint: A runbook can run each of these apps with its own commands.

form.name: Name
form.nameHint: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes, as Awak will call it.
form.urlHint: An SSH URL, like git@github.com:owner/repo.git, so the deploy key can be used.
form.subdirHint: Optional. The folder inside the repo where the app lives; empty means the root.
form.commandsHint: One command per line, no shell. Allowed programs: pnpm, npm, npx, yarn, node, python, uv, pytest, make, go, cargo. Check access fills empty fields from what it finds.

invalid.name: Use lowercase letters, digits and dashes, starting with a letter or digit.
invalid.urlHttps: Use an SSH URL (git@host:owner/repo.git). HTTPS can't use a deploy key.
invalid.branch: Enter a branch name, like main.
invalid.subdir: Use a relative path inside the repo, without ..

runbook.title: Runbook
runbook.description: How Awak installs, checks, starts and QA-tests this project's apps. Saving a runbook approves it.
runbook.unavailable: The runbook isn't reachable. Check that the Kemudi AI orchestrator is running.

empty.title: No runbook yet
empty.body: Without one, Awak runs each repository's own commands, and Browser QA works only for Kemudi's own repository.
empty.admin: Configure automatically lets Awak read the repositories, propose a runbook and prove it works. You can also paste one as JSON.
empty.member: A project admin can configure it automatically or paste one as JSON.

editor.title: Edit runbook JSON
editor.description: Kemudi checks every app, service and command before saving. Saving approves this version as you.
editor.label: Runbook JSON
editor.notObject: The runbook must be a JSON object, starting with {.

setup.title: Setup Assistant
setup.configureBusy: A setup run is in progress.
setup.cancelled: Setup cancelled. The runbook was left as it was.

status.queued: Waiting for the worker to pick this run up.
status.reading: Awak is reading the repositories and drafting a runbook.
status.fixing: The last proof failed. Awak is fixing the runbook and will prove it again.
status.needs_input: Awak needs a few values before it can prove the runbook.
status.proving: Installing, running the checks and starting the services. This can take several minutes.
status.ready: The runbook worked. Review it, then approve it to make it this project's runbook.
status.failed: Setup stopped before the runbook worked.

screenshot.title: What QA saw
screenshot.alt: Screenshot of the app's first page, taken during the proof

env.intro: These values are saved to Env & secrets for this project. Fill in what you have; the run goes on once nothing is missing.
env.writeOnly: Values are write-only here; secrets are never shown again.
env.saved: Saved. Awak goes on proving the runbook.
env.memberWait: Waiting for a project admin to fill in these values:
env.savedConfirm: Saved. Confirm the saved values above to go on.

confirm.title: Awak will use these saved values
confirm.intro: Awak's proposed runbook hands these values from Env & secrets to its own commands during the proof. Check where each one goes, then continue.
confirm.memberWait: Waiting for a project admin to let Awak use these saved values:
confirm.hint: The values stay hidden; only the proof gets them.
confirm.doneMore: Confirmed. Awak still needs a few values.

approve.browserHint: Awak will start the app and check every acceptance criterion in a browser before a story is Done.

setup.superseded: Replaced by a newer setup run. This proposal can no longer be approved.

env.title: Env & secrets
env.description: Values the runbook's services, setup commands and QA read by name. Stored encrypted and hidden from every comment, log and diff.
env.unavailable: Env values aren't reachable. Check that the Kemudi AI orchestrator is running.
env.testOnly: Test and development values only. Never enter production credentials: the project's own containers and QA can read these values.

dialog.description: Use test or development values only.
dialog.name: Name
dialog.nameHint: Capital letters, digits and _, starting with a letter or _. Names Kemudi uses itself (PATH, HOME, KEMUDI_…, GIT_…) are reserved.
dialog.nameInvalid: Use capital letters, digits and _, starting with a letter or _ (at most 64).
dialog.valueStored: A value is stored. Leave this empty to keep it.
dialog.valueHidden: Once saved, a secret value can be replaced but not shown again.
dialog.valuePlain: Project members can see this value.
dialog.valueRetype: Enter the value again: it will be shown once it is no longer secret.
dialog.secretHint: Write-only: never shown again, not even to admins.

confirmDelete.title: Delete {{name}}?
confirmDelete.desc: Services, setup commands and QA that read {{name}} will no longer get a value.

roles.title: Roles
roles.description: Each Awak role takes the stories tagged with its area, with its own model, repos and instructions.
roles.empty: No roles yet. A story is picked up only when a role covers its area.

editor.name: Name
editor.areaHint: Stories tagged area:{{area}} go to this role.
editor.areaHintBoth: Stories tagged area:both, or both area:web and area:backend, go to this role. It also takes single-area stories when no other role covers that area.
editor.modelHint: Keep the connection default, or pick another model from the same provider.
editor.reposHint: The repos this role may change. None selected means every repo.
editor.pathsHint: One relative path per line. Empty means no limit.
editor.fixedHint: Every Awak prompt starts with these rules and repeats them at the end. Your instructions can't override them.
editor.fixedAfterSave: The Kemudi rules and the role template show here once the role is saved.
editor.overlayHint: Project conventions, libraries to prefer, things to avoid. Never paste tokens or passwords; Kemudi refuses text that looks like a secret.

jobs.title: Recent jobs
jobs.description: Awak's last 50 jobs on this project. The list refreshes while a job runs.
jobs.empty: No jobs yet. Awak starts one when a Ready story has an area tag and a role covers it.

intake.title: Intake
intake.intro: Paste a brief, meeting notes or a client email, or add a document. Kemudi drafts user stories for you to check and edit, then creates them in the backlog.

agentOff.title: Awak is off for this project
agentOff.body: Stories are still created. Ready ones wait until Awak is turned on.
agentOff.link: Turn it on in Settings → Agent

source.textPlaceholder: Paste the brief, notes or email here
source.drop: Drop a PDF or DOCX here, or
source.badFile: Only PDF and DOCX files can be read.
source.drafting: Drafting stories. This can take about half a minute.

drafts.title: Drafts
drafts.summary: {{ready}} will go to Ready, {{waiting}} will wait in New. Nothing is in the backlog until you create them.
drafts.empty: The model found no stories in this text. Add more detail and draft again.
drafts.subject: Subject
drafts.keptEdits: Your drafts and edits are kept. Fix the problem and create again.

mergeButton.summary: Passed QA on {{branch}}. Waiting for an admin to merge.

confirm.title: Merge this story?
confirm.body: Kemudi merges {{branch}} into {{target}}, reruns the checks, pushes, then runs the deploy command.

mergeButton.requested: Merge requested. Waiting for the worker to pick it up.
mergeButton.merging: Merging into {{target}} and rerunning the checks.
